name: Markdown
description: A docs page, as GitHub shows its Markdown: headings with GitHub's IDs, a tip and a warning as callouts, highlighted code, a table, a list, and an image (its alt text in cells; a docs: comment before it shows nothing). It is in a HottyScrollView. Tab goes through its links in place, and Enter or a click follows one. "configuration", "FAQ" and "the top" are #fragments: the box scrolls to their heading, in cells to its top; on a HOTTY host the heading takes the focus, which scrolls it into view. "guide", "reference" and "the roadmap" are relative: each is written to /page/link, which the line under the box shows, and sends open with it, which an agent would answer with that page. "Ada Lovelace" has a scheme, so it is a hyperlink, as a Text's links are: the terminal opens it. The help line is a HottyKeyHints.

# Lovelace

Lovelace keeps notes in your terminal. Read the [guide](guide.md) first, or skip to [configuration](#configuration) and the [FAQ](#faq).

> [!TIP]
> Run `lovelace --help` to list every command.

<!-- docs:figure caption="Ada Lovelace" -->
![Ada Lovelace, after whom Lovelace is named](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a4/Ada_Lovelace_portrait.jpg/120px-Ada_Lovelace_portrait.jpg)

## Install

```sh
go install example.com/lovelace@latest
lovelace init ~/notes
```

| Platform | Package | Size |
| :-- | :-- | --: |
| macOS | Homebrew | 9 MB |
| Linux | AUR, deb, rpm | 8 MB |
| Windows | Scoop | 10 MB |

## Configuration

Settings live in `~/.config/lovelace/config.toml`; the [reference](reference/config.md) lists them all.

> [!WARNING]
> A setting that does not parse stops Lovelace at start.

1. Open the file.
2. Set `editor` to your editor.
3. Save it, and run `lovelace check`.

## FAQ

### Where are my notes?

In `~/notes`, one Markdown file a note.

### Why the name?

After [Ada Lovelace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ada_Lovelace), who wrote the first program.

### Does it sync?

Not yet: see [the roadmap](roadmap.md). Back to [the top](#lovelace).
